services.name: American Truck Simulator
services.description: SCS Software's American Truck Simulator convoy dedicated server, installed through SteamCMD.

settings.prompt: Steam Game Server Login Token (empty for a temporary server ID)
settings.description: Create one at steamcommunity.com/dev/managegameservers with app ID 270880, so the server keeps the same ID across restarts.

services.name: Core Keeper
services.description: Pugstorm's Core Keeper dedicated server, installed through SteamCMD and run on a virtual display.

ports.name: game
ports.description: Direct connections. Players normally join with the Game ID through Steam's relay, so forwarding is optional.

notes: Needs xvfb-run on the host, because the server won't start without a display.
Players join with the Game ID the server writes to GameID.txt in the server folder.

services.name: Counter-Strike 2
services.description: Valve's Counter-Strike 2 dedicated server, installed through SteamCMD (about 35 GB).

settings.prompt: RCON password (leave empty to generate one)
Game Server Login Token (empty for a LAN-only server)
settings.description: Create one at steamcommunity.com/dev/managegameservers with app ID 730.

services.name: CryoFall
services.description: AtomicTorch's CryoFall dedicated server, a .NET server installed through SteamCMD.

linuxgsm.notes: Not in LinuxGSM. Sourced from the Pelican/Pterodactyl egg.

notes: Needs the .NET 6 runtime on the host.
Server name, password and port live in Data/SettingsServer.xml, which the server creates on first start. Anyserve can't edit XML yet, so change them there; the game port setting above must match it.

services.name: Don't Starve Together
services.description: Klei's Don't Starve Together dedicated server (surface shard only), installed through SteamCMD.

settings.prompt: Klei cluster token (from accounts.klei.com, Games, Game Servers)
settings.description: Every DST server needs a token tied to your Klei account.

files.template:
[GAMEPLAY]
game_mode = survival

[NETWORK]
cluster_name = Anyserve

[MISC]
console_enabled = true

[SHARD]
shard_enabled = false

notes: Surface world only. The Caves shard is a second server process, which Anyserve can't run as part of one service yet.

services.name: Killing Floor
services.description: Tripwire's original Killing Floor dedicated server, installed through SteamCMD with a Steam account.

settings.prompt: Admin password for web admin (leave empty to generate one)

notes: Needs a Steam account that owns Killing Floor. Sign in once with `anyserve steam login <user>`; SteamCMD keeps the session and Anyserve never sees the password.

services.name: Lemmy
services.description: A federated link aggregator and forum (like Reddit, on the fediverse), as a stack of containers.

settings.prompt: Domain name people will use (e.g. lemmy.example.com)
settings.description: Federation uses this name, and it can't be changed after the first start.

settings.prompt: Will it be served over HTTPS by a proxy in front of it?
settings.description: Say no only for testing on this machine. Federation needs HTTPS.

settings.prompt: Admin user name (created on first start)
Admin password, 10 to 60 characters (leave empty to generate one)
Database password (leave empty to generate one)
Image server API key (leave empty to generate one)

ports.name: http
ports.description: The whole site (UI, API, images, federation). Put an HTTPS proxy in front of it.

exec.description: the PostgreSQL shell for Lemmy's database

linuxgsm.notes: Not a game server, so it doesn't belong in LinuxGSM.

notes: Needs Docker with the Compose plugin.
The site listens on 127.0.0.1 only. Put an HTTPS reverse proxy (Caddy, nginx, a tunnel) in front of it for your domain.
The admin account is created on the first start; `anyserve info` doesn't show generated passwords, but they're in the instance's instance.json.

services.name: No One Survived
services.description: No One Survived zombie survival dedicated server (Windows build), installed through SteamCMD.

settings.prompt: Admin password (leave empty to generate one)

linuxgsm.notes: Windows-only server, so it can't go into LinuxGSM without Wine. Sourced from the Pelican/Pterodactyl egg, which runs it under Wine.

notes: Windows only; Anyserve doesn't run Windows servers under Wine.
The server writes Engine.ini and Game.ini on first start; Anyserve applies your settings from the second start on.

services.name: Plains of Pain
services.description: Plains of Pain survival dedicated server, installed through SteamCMD.

settings.default: An Anyserve Plains of Pain server

settings.prompt: World size (used only when the world is first created)
Server password (letters, digits, - and _; empty for none)

linuxgsm.notes: Not in LinuxGSM. Sourced from the Pelican/Pterodactyl egg.

notes: Saves live under .config/unity3d in the server folder, because Anyserve gives each server its own home.

services.name: Quake 4
services.description: id Software's Quake 4 dedicated server (1.4.2), from LinuxGSM's archive of the official Linux build.

settings.prompt: Remote console password (leave empty to generate one)

files.template:
// Your own Quake 4 server settings. Anyserve never changes this file.
set si_warmup 1
set si_fragLimit 25
set si_timeLimit 15

notes: Bring your own game data. The archive holds the 1.4.2 server and patch paks, but not the base game's q4base/pak001.pk4 to pak012.pk4, which aren't redistributable. Copy those from your own copy of Quake 4 (Steam app 2210) into q4base, or the server stops with "Couldn't load scripts/main.script".
The server crashes on start if its folder path is very long (over about 100 characters); the default location is fine.
A 32-bit server. On 64-bit Debian or Ubuntu it needs the 32-bit C library (sudo apt install libc6-i386).

services.name: Rust
services.description: Facepunch's Rust dedicated server, installed through SteamCMD.

settings.prompt: Server name (shown in the server browser)

notes: The server download is about 10 GB, and the first start builds the map, which takes several minutes.
Facepunch pushes a forced update on the first Thursday of each month. Run `anyserve update` then.
No native macOS server exists. Use the container target on a Mac.

services.name: Stationeers
services.description: RocketWerkz's Stationeers dedicated server, installed through SteamCMD.

settings.description: Used only when the save is first created.

services.name: Terraria
services.description: Re-Logic's official vanilla Terraria dedicated server.

settings.prompt: World size (used only when the world is first created)
Difficulty (used only when the world is first created)

settings.default: Welcome to an Anyserve Terraria server!

notes: Vanilla server only. A TShock variant is planned.
The world is created on first start, which can take a minute.

services.name: Wurm Unlimited
services.description: Code Club AB's Wurm Unlimited dedicated server, run headless without the GUI launcher.

settings.prompt: Server name (shown in the server browser)
Home kingdom (Adventure only; Creative always uses Freedom)
Use Epic cluster rules (Epic skill curve)?
IP address to bind (leave empty to let the server choose)

linuxgsm.notes: Not in LinuxGSM as far as we know. This is the first planned contribution.

notes: The headless launch arguments come from the original wurm_unlimited_server scripts.
Known issue on Linux: the server's bundled Java crashes inside Steam's library when it shuts down. Whether the last moments of play are saved hasn't been checked yet, so back up before stopping.
The Windows launch has not been tested yet.
No native macOS server exists. Use the container target on a Mac.
